title: Matrix transformations
summary: A [[transformation-matrix|transformation matrix]] moves every point of a shape at once: $\boldsymbol{x}' = A\boldsymbol{x} + \boldsymbol{b}$ can stretch, enlarge, rotate, reflect and translate. Multiplying matrices combines moves, repeating them builds [[fractal|fractals]], and $\lvert\det A\rvert$ scales areas.

goals.text: Transform points with $\boldsymbol{x}' = A\boldsymbol{x} + \boldsymbol{b}$: stretches, enlargements and [[translation|translations]].
Write down and describe matrices for rotations and [[reflection|reflections]].
Combine transformations into one [[matrix|matrix]], in the right order.
Repeat transformations to make spirals and fractals.
Use $\lvert\det A\rvert$ to find the area of an image or of the original shape.

before.hint: Row 1 times the column gives the top entry; row 2 times the column gives the bottom one.
before.explain: Top: $3(5) + (-2)(2) = 11$. Bottom: $1(5) + 4(2) = 13$. Using the columns instead of the rows gives $\begin{pmatrix}17\\-2\end{pmatrix}$. Revise it in {{lesson:1.14}}.

before.hint: $\det A = ad - bc$. Watch the signs.

blocks.text: In {{lesson:2.8}} you transformed graphs. Now you move points. Write each point $(x, y)$ as a column $\begin{pmatrix}x\\y\end{pmatrix}$, and one matrix moves every point of a shape at once.
For example, $\begin{pmatrix}3 & 0\\0 & 2\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}x\\y\end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix}3x\\2y\end{pmatrix}$. Every $x$-coordinate is tripled and every $y$-coordinate doubled.

blocks.statement: The transformation $\begin{pmatrix}x'\\y'\end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix}a & b\\c & d\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}x\\y\end{pmatrix} + \begin{pmatrix}e\\f\end{pmatrix}$, or $\boldsymbol{x}' = A\boldsymbol{x} + \boldsymbol{b}$, maps each point $(x, y)$ to its image $(x', y')$. $A$ is the transformation matrix and $\boldsymbol{b}$ is a translation vector.
blocks.plain: A matrix that tells every point where to go.

blocks.text: The matrix acts first, then the translation slides every point $e$ across and $f$ up.

The columns of $A$ are the images of $(1, 0)$ and $(0, 1)$: $A\begin{pmatrix}1\\0\end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix}a\\c\end{pmatrix}$ and $A\begin{pmatrix}0\\1\end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix}b\\d\end{pmatrix}$. To find a matrix, ask where those two points go.
With no translation, $A\begin{pmatrix}0\\0\end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix}0\\0\end{pmatrix}$: the origin is [[invariant|invariant]]. So every booklet matrix acts relative to the origin.

These are in the booklet. A [[horizontal-stretch|horizontal stretch]] multiplies each $x$-coordinate by $k$ and fixes the $y$-axis. A [[vertical-stretch|vertical stretch]] does the same to $y$ and fixes the $x$-axis.

blocks.question: A photo app stores a sticker's corner at $(6, 4)$. The app moves every point by $\begin{pmatrix}x'\\y'\end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix}1.5 & 0\\0 & 1.5\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}x\\y\end{pmatrix} + \begin{pmatrix}-2\\3\end{pmatrix}$. Describe the transformation, and find the new position of the corner.
steps: The matrix is the enlargement form with $k = 1.5$: an enlargement, scale factor $1.5$, centre $(0, 0)$. The vector then translates every point by $\begin{pmatrix}-2\\3\end{pmatrix}$.
Multiply first: $\begin{pmatrix}1.5 & 0\\0 & 1.5\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}6\\4\end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix}9\\6\end{pmatrix}$.
Then add the translation: $\begin{pmatrix}9 - 2\\6 + 3\end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix}7\\9\end{pmatrix}$.
Interpret: the corner moves to $(7, 9)$, and every length on the sticker is $1.5$ times longer.

blocks.question: A design tool uses $\boldsymbol{x}' = A\boldsymbol{x} + \boldsymbol{b}$. It maps $(0, 0)$ to $(-2, 5)$, $(1, 0)$ to $(1, 5)$ and $(0, 1)$ to $(-2, 5.5)$. Find $\boldsymbol{b}$ and $A$, describe $A$, and find the image of $(4, -2)$.
steps: The origin maps to $\boldsymbol{b}$, so $\boldsymbol{b} = \begin{pmatrix}-2\\5\end{pmatrix}$.
Subtract $\boldsymbol{b}$ from the other images: $A\begin{pmatrix}1\\0\end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix}3\\0\end{pmatrix}$ and $A\begin{pmatrix}0\\1\end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix}0\\0.5\end{pmatrix}$.
These are the columns, so $A = \begin{pmatrix}3 & 0\\0 & 0.5\end{pmatrix}$: a horizontal stretch, scale factor $3$, and a vertical stretch, scale factor $0.5$.

Image of $(4, -2)$: $\begin{pmatrix}3 & 0\\0 & 0.5\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}4\\-2\end{pmatrix} + \begin{pmatrix}-2\\5\end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix}12\\-1\end{pmatrix} + \begin{pmatrix}-2\\5\end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix}10\\4\end{pmatrix}$.

blocks.text: Adding the translation before multiplying. In $A\boldsymbol{x} + \boldsymbol{b}$ the matrix acts first; $A(\boldsymbol{x} + \boldsymbol{b})$ is a different transformation.

blocks.prompt: Under the matrix $\begin{pmatrix}4 & -1\\2 & 3\end{pmatrix}$, what is the image of $(0, 1)$?
blocks.hint: The image of $(0, 1)$ is one of the columns.
blocks.explain: It is the second column. $(4, 2)$ is the image of $(1, 0)$; $(4, -1)$ is a row.

blocks.prompt: The matrix $\begin{pmatrix}2 & 1\\1 & 1\end{pmatrix}$ maps a point $P$ to $(7, 4)$. Find $P$.
blocks.hint: Undo the matrix with its [[inverse-matrix|inverse]]: $P = A^{-1}\begin{pmatrix}7\\4\end{pmatrix}$.
blocks.explain: $\det A = 2 - 1 = 1$, so $A^{-1} = \begin{pmatrix}1 & -1\\-1 & 2\end{pmatrix}$ and $A^{-1}\begin{pmatrix}7\\4\end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix}3\\1\end{pmatrix}$. $(18, 11)$ applies $A$ again instead of undoing it.

blocks.text: Turn $(1, 0)$ anticlockwise through $\theta$ about the origin: it lands on $(\cos\theta, \sin\theta)$. $(0, 1)$ lands on $(-\sin\theta, \cos\theta)$. These images are the columns of the rotation matrix.

blocks.tex: \begin{pmatrix}\cos\theta & -\sin\theta\\\sin\theta & \cos\theta\end{pmatrix}:\ \text{anticlockwise rotation of angle } \theta \text{ about the origin } (\theta > 0)
\begin{pmatrix}\cos\theta & \sin\theta\\-\sin\theta & \cos\theta\end{pmatrix}:\ \text{clockwise rotation of angle } \theta \text{ about the origin } (\theta > 0)

blocks.text: The two rotation matrices differ only in the signs of $\sin\theta$. A clockwise turn of $\theta$ is an anticlockwise turn of $-\theta$.
The mirror line passes through the origin, and $\theta$ is its angle with the positive $x$-axis. The matrix uses $2\theta$, not $\theta$.

For the $x$-axis, $\theta = 0^{\circ}$ gives $\begin{pmatrix}1 & 0\\0 & -1\end{pmatrix}$. For the line $y = x$, $\theta = 45^{\circ}$ gives $\begin{pmatrix}0 & 1\\1 & 0\end{pmatrix}$. For the $y$-axis, $\theta = 90^{\circ}$ gives $\begin{pmatrix}-1 & 0\\0 & 1\end{pmatrix}$, even though $\tan 90^{\circ}$ is undefined. All four rotation and reflection formulas are in the booklet.

blocks.question: The tip of a wind-turbine blade is at $(0, 42)$, in metres, relative to the hub at the origin. The blade turns $50^{\circ}$ clockwise about the hub. Find the new position of the tip, to 3 s.f.
steps: Clockwise, so use $\begin{pmatrix}\cos\theta & \sin\theta\\-\sin\theta & \cos\theta\end{pmatrix}$ with $\theta = 50^{\circ}$. Set the GDC to degrees.

Write down the product: $\begin{pmatrix}\cos 50^{\circ} & \sin 50^{\circ}\\-\sin 50^{\circ} & \cos 50^{\circ}\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}0\\42\end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix}42\sin 50^{\circ}\\42\cos 50^{\circ}\end{pmatrix}$.
Evaluate: $42\sin 50^{\circ} = 32.173\ldots$ and $42\cos 50^{\circ} = 26.997\ldots$
Check: $\sqrt{32.173\ldots^{2} + 26.997\ldots^{2}} = 42$, as a rotation keeps distances.
Interpret: the tip is now $32.2$ m to the right of the hub and $27.0$ m above it.

blocks.question: A garden is symmetric about a straight path along the line $y = 3x$. A tree stands at $(10, 5)$. Use a reflection matrix to find where its mirror image stands.
steps: The path makes angle $\theta$ with the $x$-axis, with $\tan\theta = 3$. So $\theta = \tan^{-1} 3 = 71.565\ldots^{\circ}$ and $2\theta = 143.130\ldots^{\circ}$.
The GDC gives $\cos 2\theta = -0.8$ and $\sin 2\theta = 0.6$ exactly, so the matrix is $\begin{pmatrix}-0.8 & 0.6\\0.6 & 0.8\end{pmatrix}$.
Multiply: $\begin{pmatrix}-0.8 & 0.6\\0.6 & 0.8\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}10\\5\end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix}-8 + 3\\6 + 4\end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix}-5\\10\end{pmatrix}$.
Check: the midpoint of $(10, 5)$ and $(-5, 10)$ is $(2.5, 7.5)$, and $7.5 = 3 \times 2.5$: it lies on the path, as it must.

blocks.text: Using $\theta$ instead of $2\theta$ in the reflection matrix. Test a point: its midpoint with its image lies on the mirror line.

blocks.prompt: Describe fully the transformation with matrix $\begin{pmatrix}0 & 1\\-1 & 0\end{pmatrix}$.
blocks.hint: Find the images of $(1, 0)$ and $(0, 1)$: they are the columns.

options.text: a clockwise rotation of 90 degrees about the origin
an anticlockwise rotation of 90 degrees about the origin
a reflection in the line y = x

blocks.explain: $(1, 0)$ goes to $(0, -1)$ and $(0, 1)$ goes to $(1, 0)$: each turns a quarter-turn clockwise. It is the clockwise matrix with $\theta = 90^{\circ}$.

verify.truth: a clockwise rotation of 90 degrees about the origin

blocks.prompt: Which matrix reflects points in the line $y = -x$?
blocks.hint: The line makes $\theta = 135^{\circ}$ with the positive $x$-axis, so $2\theta = 270^{\circ}$.
blocks.explain: $\cos 270^{\circ} = 0$ and $\sin 270^{\circ} = -1$ give $\begin{pmatrix}0 & -1\\-1 & 0\end{pmatrix}$. Check: $(1, 0)$ goes to $(0, -1)$, its mirror image in $y = -x$. The second option reflects in $y = x$; the third is a rotation.

blocks.text: Apply $A$ to a point, then apply $B$ to its image. The result is $B(A\boldsymbol{x}) = (BA)\boldsymbol{x}$, so the single matrix $BA$ does both.

blocks.statement: Transformation $A$ followed by transformation $B$ has the single matrix $BA$: the first one goes on the right. With translations, $\boldsymbol{x}' = A\boldsymbol{x} + \boldsymbol{a}$ followed by $\boldsymbol{x}'' = B\boldsymbol{x}' + \boldsymbol{b}$ gives $\boldsymbol{x}'' = BA\boldsymbol{x} + B\boldsymbol{a} + \boldsymbol{b}$.
blocks.why: The matrix next to $\boldsymbol{x}$ acts on it first, and in general $AB \neq BA$.

blocks.question: A drawing app rotates a shape $90^{\circ}$ anticlockwise about the origin, then reflects the result in the $x$-axis. Find the single matrix for the combined transformation, and describe it fully.
steps: Rotation, $\theta = 90^{\circ}$ anticlockwise: $R = \begin{pmatrix}0 & -1\\1 & 0\end{pmatrix}$. Reflection in the $x$-axis: $M = \begin{pmatrix}1 & 0\\0 & -1\end{pmatrix}$.
$R$ acts first, so it goes on the right: $MR = \begin{pmatrix}1 & 0\\0 & -1\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}0 & -1\\1 & 0\end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix}0 & -1\\-1 & 0\end{pmatrix}$.
Match the reflection form: $\cos 2\theta = 0$ and $\sin 2\theta = -1$ give $\theta = 135^{\circ}$. So it is a reflection in $y = -x$.
Check: $(1, 0)$ rotates to $(0, 1)$, then reflects to $(0, -1)$, the first column of $MR$.
The other order, $RM = \begin{pmatrix}0 & 1\\1 & 0\end{pmatrix}$, is a reflection in $y = x$: a different answer.

blocks.prompt: A shape is reflected using matrix $Y$, then stretched using matrix $S$. Which single matrix gives the combined transformation?
blocks.hint: The transformation applied first sits next to $\boldsymbol{x}$.
blocks.explain: $S(Y\boldsymbol{x}) = (SY)\boldsymbol{x}$: reflect first, so $Y$ is on the right. Adding matrices doesn't combine transformations.

blocks.text: Now repeat one transformation. With $\boldsymbol{x}_{1} = A\boldsymbol{x}_{0}$, $\boldsymbol{x}_{2} = A\boldsymbol{x}_{1} = A^{2}\boldsymbol{x}_{0}$ and so on, the point after $n$ steps is $\boldsymbol{x}_{n} = A^{n}\boldsymbol{x}_{0}$. Your GDC's matrix power jumps straight there.
A rotation of $30^{\circ}$ applied $12$ times is a full turn of $360^{\circ}$, so its 12th power is the [[identity-matrix|identity matrix]] $I$.

blocks.question: An animation moves a dot by the matrix $C = 0.9\begin{pmatrix}\cos 30^{\circ} & -\sin 30^{\circ}\\\sin 30^{\circ} & \cos 30^{\circ}\end{pmatrix}$ once every frame. The dot starts at $P_{0}(10, 0)$. (a) Describe $C$ fully. (b) Use your GDC to find its position $P_{8}$ after $8$ frames, to 3 s.f.
steps: (a) An enlargement, scale factor $0.9$, centre $(0, 0)$, and an anticlockwise rotation of $30^{\circ}$ about the origin. An enlargement $kI$ commutes with every matrix, so their order doesn't matter.
(b) In degree mode, enter $C$ with exact entries such as $0.9\cos 30^{\circ}$, so nothing is rounded.
Write down what you enter, $C^{8}\begin{pmatrix}10\\0\end{pmatrix}$. The GDC gives $\begin{pmatrix}-2.1523\ldots\\-3.7279\ldots\end{pmatrix}$.
Check: $8$ frames turn the dot $240^{\circ}$ and scale its distance by $0.9^{8}$, giving $10(0.9^{8})(\cos 240^{\circ}, \sin 240^{\circ})$.
Interpret: each frame the dot turns $30^{\circ}$ and gets $10\%$ closer to the origin: it spirals in.

blocks.alt: Axes from minus 10 to 10. Thirteen dots spiral anticlockwise in towards the origin, joined by a dashed line. P0 is at (10, 0). P8 is below and to the left of the origin, at about (minus 2.15, minus 3.73). P12 is back on the positive x-axis, closer to the origin.
blocks.caption: Each frame turns the dot $30^{\circ}$ and multiplies its distance from the origin by $0.9$.

blocks.text: Then multiply $C^{8}$ by $\begin{pmatrix}10\\0\end{pmatrix}$, or take its first column times $10$.

blocks.prompt: In the animation, the dot is first back on the positive $x$-axis after $12$ frames. How far from the origin is it then? Give 3 s.f.
blocks.hint: Each frame multiplies the distance from the origin by $0.9$.
blocks.explain: $12 \times 30^{\circ} = 360^{\circ}$, a full turn, and the distance is $10(0.9^{12}) = 2.824\ldots \approx 2.82$.

blocks.text: A [[fractal|fractal]] repeats a set of transformations for ever. Each stage replaces every piece with smaller transformed copies, giving detail at every scale.

blocks.alt: Three right-angled triangles side by side, each with the right angle at the bottom left. Stage 0 is one shaded triangle. Stage 1 has three shaded half-size triangles, in the bottom-left, bottom-right and top corners, with the middle part empty. Stage 2 repeats this inside each of the three, giving nine shaded quarter-size triangles.
blocks.caption: Stages $0$, $1$ and $2$: each triangle is replaced by its images under three maps.

blocks.question: A fractal starts with the triangle with vertices $(0, 0)$, $(16, 0)$ and $(0, 16)$, in cm. Each stage applies $T_{1}: \boldsymbol{x}' = 0.5\boldsymbol{x}$, $T_{2}: \boldsymbol{x}' = 0.5\boldsymbol{x} + \begin{pmatrix}8\\0\end{pmatrix}$ and $T_{3}: \boldsymbol{x}' = 0.5\boldsymbol{x} + \begin{pmatrix}0\\8\end{pmatrix}$ to every triangle, and keeps only the images. (a) Find the image of the starting triangle under $T_{2}$. (b) Find the shaded area after $5$ stages.
steps: (a) $T_{2}$ halves each vertex, then adds $8$ to $x$: $(0, 0) \mapsto (8, 0)$, $(16, 0) \mapsto (16, 0)$, $(0, 16) \mapsto (8, 8)$. That is the bottom-right copy.
(b) The start has area $\frac{1}{2}(16)(16) = 128\text{ cm}^{2}$. Each map is an enlargement with scale factor $0.5$, so each copy has $0.5^{2} = \frac{1}{4}$ of its parent's area.

The three copies don't overlap, so each stage keeps $3 \times \frac{1}{4} = \frac{3}{4}$ of the area. The areas $128, 96, 72, \dots$ form a [[geometric-sequence|geometric sequence]] with $r = \frac{3}{4}$.
After $5$ stages: $128\left(\frac{3}{4}\right)^{5} = 30.375\text{ cm}^{2}$.
Interpret: the areas removed, $32, 24, 18, \dots$, have [[sum-to-infinity|sum to infinity]] $\frac{32}{1 - 0.75} = 128$. In the limit the shaded area shrinks to $0$.

blocks.prompt: Each stage of a fractal replaces every square with $8$ non-overlapping copies, each enlarged by scale factor $\frac{1}{3}$. What fraction of the area is left after $4$ stages? Give 3 s.f.
blocks.hint: Each copy has $\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^{2}$ of its parent's area.
blocks.explain: Each stage keeps $8 \times \frac{1}{9} = \frac{8}{9}$ of the area, so after $4$ stages $\left(\frac{8}{9}\right)^{4} = 0.6242\ldots \approx 0.624$.

blocks.text: Under $A = \begin{pmatrix}3 & 1\\1 & 2\end{pmatrix}$, the unit square becomes a parallelogram with sides along the columns $(3, 1)$ and $(1, 2)$.

blocks.alt: Axes from 0 to 4 across and 0 to 3 up. A small shaded unit square with corners (0, 0), (1, 0), (1, 1) and (0, 1) is labelled 1. A larger shaded parallelogram with corners (0, 0), (3, 1), (4, 3) and (1, 2) is labelled area 5.
blocks.caption: The unit square's image has area $\det A = 3(2) - 1(1) = 5$.

blocks.statement: When a shape is transformed by $\boldsymbol{x}' = A\boldsymbol{x} + \boldsymbol{b}$, area of image $= \lvert\det A\rvert \times$ area of object. The translation $\boldsymbol{b}$ doesn't change the area.
blocks.why: Every small square in the shape becomes a parallelogram scaled by the same factor, $\lvert ad - bc\rvert$.

blocks.text: So the [[determinant|determinant]]'s size, $\lvert\det A\rvert$, is the area scale factor. Rotations and reflections keep area: $\lvert\det A\rvert = 1$. An enlargement $kI$ has $\det = k^{2}$; a stretch has $\det = k$.
If $\det A < 0$, the image is also flipped over. If $\det A = 0$, the shape is squashed onto a line (or a single point), and $A$ has no inverse.
Two transformations in turn multiply their area factors: $\det(BA) = \det B \times \det A$.

blocks.question: A logo of area $15\text{ cm}^{2}$ is transformed by $\begin{pmatrix}2 & -1\\3 & 1.5\end{pmatrix}$. Find the area of the image.
steps: Area of image $= \lvert 6\rvert \times 15 = 90\text{ cm}^{2}$.
Interpret: the image covers $6$ times the logo's area.

blocks.question: A design of area $8\text{ m}^{2}$ is transformed by $M = \begin{pmatrix}k & 2\\3 & k\end{pmatrix}$, where $k > 0$. The image has area $40\text{ m}^{2}$. Find the possible values of $k$.
steps: $\det M = k^{2} - 6$, so $\lvert k^{2} - 6\rvert \times 8 = 40$, which gives $\lvert k^{2} - 6\rvert = 5$.
Keep only $k > 0$: $k = \sqrt{11}$ or $k = 1$.
Check $k = 1$: $\det M = 1 - 6 = -5$, and $\lvert -5\rvert \times 8 = 40$. The image is flipped, but its area is still $40\text{ m}^{2}$.

blocks.text: Dropping the modulus. Area uses $\lvert\det A\rvert$, so a negative determinant still gives a positive area, and $\lvert\det A\rvert = c$ has two cases. Then keep only the values the question allows.

blocks.prompt: A triangle is transformed by $\begin{pmatrix}4 & -1\\2 & 3\end{pmatrix}$, and its image has area $54\text{ cm}^{2}$. Find the area of the original triangle, in $\text{cm}^{2}$, to 3 s.f.
blocks.hint: Divide the image's area by $\lvert\det A\rvert$.
blocks.explain: $\det A = 4(3) - (-1)(2) = 14$, so the original area is $\frac{54}{14} = 3.857\ldots \approx 3.86\text{ cm}^{2}$.

blocks.prompt: A shape of area $12\text{ cm}^{2}$ is enlarged by scale factor $3$, centre O, then rotated $40^{\circ}$ about O. Find the area of the final image, in $\text{cm}^{2}$.
blocks.explain: The enlargement has $\det = 3^{2} = 9$; the rotation has $\det = \cos^{2} 40^{\circ} + \sin^{2} 40^{\circ} = 1$. So the area is $9 \times 12 = 108\text{ cm}^{2}$. $36$ uses $3$, not $3^{2}$; $82.7$ wrongly multiplies by $\cos 40^{\circ}$, but a rotation keeps area.

blocks.text: $\boldsymbol{x}' = A\boldsymbol{x} + \boldsymbol{b}$: the matrix acts first, then the translation $\boldsymbol{b}$. The columns of $A$ are the images of $(1, 0)$ and $(0, 1)$.
The booklet's rotations are about the origin, with $\theta > 0$. Its reflection matrix uses $2\theta$, where the mirror line $y = (\tan\theta)x$ passes through the origin.
Transformation $A$ followed by transformation $B$ has the single matrix $BA$: the first one goes on the right.
With no translation, applying $A$ $n$ times gives $\boldsymbol{x}_{n} = A^{n}\boldsymbol{x}_{0}$.

Area of image $= \lvert\det A\rvert \times$ area of object for $\boldsymbol{x}' = A\boldsymbol{x} + \boldsymbol{b}$; translations don't change area. For $A$ then $B$, $\det(BA) = \det B \times \det A$.
A fractal stage making $m$ non-overlapping copies of each piece, each with area factor $\lvert\det A\rvert$, multiplies the area by $m\lvert\det A\rvert$: a geometric sequence.

mistakes: Multiplying in the wrong order. $A$ followed by $B$ is $BA$; the right matrices in the wrong order lose the accuracy mark.
Using the anticlockwise matrix for a clockwise turn. Check the direction, then test the point $(1, 0)$.
Putting $\theta$ instead of $2\theta$ into the reflection matrix. Here $\theta$ is the mirror line's angle with the positive $x$-axis.
Forgetting the modulus in area $= \lvert\det A\rvert \times$ area. An equation in $\lvert\det A\rvert$ has two cases; give only the values the question allows.
Rounding entries such as $\cos 30^{\circ}$ before taking powers. Enter exact entries, in the right angle mode, and round only the final answer.
examTips: "Describe fully" a transformation: name it and give every detail. Rotation: angle, direction, centre. Enlargement or stretch: scale factor, and centre or direction. Reflection: the mirror line.
"Write down" a matrix: substitute into the booklet form, with the angle and direction the question gives.
"Find" with the GDC: write down the product or power you entered, such as $C^{8}\boldsymbol{x}_{0}$, then the answer to 3 s.f. A bare GDC answer can lose the method marks.
